value: Three scopes: project, global, auto. Auto uses project if .reverie/ (or legacy .codexcli.json) exists. Single-key lookups fall through project -> global. STORE OF ORIGIN (#292, owner decision for #280): a reference resolves in the store of the entry that holds it — a global entry's dollar-brace and dollar-paren refs, and the aliases they name, read only the global store; a project entry's read project, then global. Every read path follows it (run, get, find, lint, set's warning, MCP get/set); getValueWithStore reports which store a value came from. With -G a typed name resolves through the GLOBAL aliases only (#284), on every command that takes a key; MCP scope "global" and `run -G` already did. Without -G, project aliases apply and writes land in the project store. EXPLICIT PROJECT SCOPE (#298): -P / MCP scope "project" with no project refuses (PROJECT_UNRESOLVED) everywhere, reads and runs included — never a fallback to the global store. Where the store's cached project lookup and a fresh one disagree (an MCP server started before `rvr init`, an unmigratable .codexcli.json) an unscoped write refuses and every run asks. ONE RESOLVER (step 2 of the 1.4.0 plan): src/utils/nameResolver.ts resolveName(view, context, name) is the only code that decides what a name means — typed (default scope, -G, MCP scope omitted/global/project), a reference (store of origin), a chain member — and returns the key, the scope, and the names the run gate checks. It is pure; alias.ts builds the view lazily, because loading a store has effects (unreadable-file reports, legacy migration). name-resolver-boundary.test.ts fails on a name decided outside alias.ts. ALIAS LISTS (#260): an alias command changes only the list of the store it writes. A default-scope rename re-points the project's aliases and names each global alias it left; a default-scope alias removal is project-only, and a global-only alias refuses NOT_FOUND pointing at -G. Show "no change" with scripts/scope-differential (0 differences); declare intended differences with --expect.
